name: Egg
visibility: May be visible as specks; reliable identification needs magnification. A 10x hand lens is a proposed field aid and remains unverified in the current source set.
seasonality: Possible on fresh flush; stage-specific Punjab month evidence is incomplete.
immediateAction: Confirm identity with magnification and inspect for nymphs or adults before considering treatment.
managementEvidence: No egg-specific formulation or action rule is verified in the current PAU source.

name: Nymph
visibility: Later nymphs can be found with careful naked-eye inspection; use magnification for reliable early-stage identification.
seasonality: Psylla is within PAU's March-mid-October peak period.
immediateAction: Count infested shoots, inspect natural enemies, and compare repeated observations.
managementEvidence: PAU lists imidacloprid 17.8% SL, thiamethoxam 25% WG, horticultural mineral oil, and specified vegetable-oil treatments for citrus psylla. These require current-label, interval, flowering, water-stress, and recent-IRAC checks.

name: Adult
visibility: Generally observable during careful visual scouting; identification needs comparison with verified images.
seasonality: Possible year-round; actual orchard scouting outweighs the calendar.
immediateAction: Inspect fresh flush for eggs and nymphs. Distinguish isolated migrant adults from an increasing orchard-wide population.
managementEvidence: PAU lists general citrus-psylla options, but no adult-only formulation ranking, threshold, or repeat-spray interval is verified.

name: Associated damage
visibility: Visible symptoms can be inspected with the naked eye, but they are not unique to psylla.
seasonality: Damage may be observed whenever an active psylla population is established on susceptible flush.
identificationNotes: Inspect for leaf curl, drying shoots, waxy or honeydew-like deposits, and greening symptoms. Lacewing eggs on fine stalks and clustered ladybird eggs can be beneficial; do not treat them as psylla.
immediateAction: Use the assessment workflow with counts, trend, previous products, crop condition, and local context.
managementEvidence: Mixed stages or damage alone cannot create a treatment schedule. Evaluate documented options only after identification and scouting.
